item.title: Elder Kuṭivihāri: Who is in the hut? A bhikkhu free from greed, His mind well concentrated. Know him, O good sir, The hut you built…
item.description:
Elder Kuṭivihāri:

Who is in the hut? A bhikkhu free from greed,
His mind well concentrated. Know him, O good sir,
The hut you built is not in vain.

From: Theragāthā 1.56

item.title: Bhikkhus, for one who has developed and cultivated mindfulness of the body, whatever wholesome states are internal all belong to the component of true knowledge.…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, for one who has developed and cultivated mindfulness of the body, whatever wholesome states are internal all belong to the component of true knowledge. Just as, bhikkhus, the great ocean, if one pervades it with the mind, all rivers that flow into it belong to the great ocean. So too, bhikkhus, for one who has developed and cultivated mindfulness of the body, whatever wholesome states are internal all belong to the component of true knowledge.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 119 – Kāyagatāsatisutta

item.title: ( Yakkha ): How to cross the flood? How to cross the great ocean? How to escape suffering? How to be purified? ( Blessed One…
item.description:
( Yakkha ):
How to cross the flood?
How to cross the great ocean?
How to escape suffering?
How to be purified?

( Blessed One ):
With faith, cross the flood.
With heedfulness, cross the ocean.
With energy, escape suffering.
With wisdom, be purified.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 10.12

item.title: From whom a person learns the Dhamma, Let him pay homage to that person as the devas pay homage to Inda. That one, being honored,…
item.description:
From whom a person learns the Dhamma,
Let him pay homage to that person as the devas pay homage to Inda.
That one, being honored, with joyful mind,
Having learned much, proclaims the true Dhamma.

An attentive, wise person, reflecting,
Practicing Dhamma in accordance with Dhamma,
Becomes learned, intelligent, and careful.
By serving such a one, he becomes not heedless.

From: Sutta Nipāta 2.8

item.title: Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons exist and are found in the world. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a person has attained internal serenity of mind…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons exist and are found in the world. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a person has attained internal serenity of mind but not the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. Here, bhikkhus, a person has attained the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena but not internal serenity of mind. Here, bhikkhus, a person has attained neither internal serenity of mind nor the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. Here, bhikkhus, a person has attained both internal serenity of mind and the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons exist and are found in the world.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.92

item.title: The evil-doer sees it as good As long as evil has not ripened. But when evil ripens, The evil-doer sees the evil. Do not overlook…
item.description:
The evil-doer sees it as good
As long as evil has not ripened.
But when evil ripens,
The evil-doer sees the evil.

Do not overlook evil,
Thinking 'It will not come to me.'
By the falling of water drops,
A water jar is filled.
The fool becomes full of evil,
Accumulating it little by little.

Do not overlook good,
Thinking 'It will not come to me.'
By the falling of water drops,
A water jar is filled.
The wise person becomes full of good,
Accumulating it little by little.

From: Dhammapada 116-128

item.title: Speak to him of the excellent Dhamma, Not speaking divisively, not disparaging anyone. But there are those who engage in verbal battles, Little-minded people —…
item.description:
Speak to him of the excellent Dhamma,
Not speaking divisively, not disparaging anyone.

But there are those who engage in verbal battles,
Little-minded people — we do not praise them.
Fetters bind them here and there;
They lead the mind too far.

From: Sutta Nipāta 2.14

item.title: - This saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning, bhikkhus. A first point is not discerned of beings roaming and wandering on, shrouded by ignorance and fettered…
item.description:
- This saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning, bhikkhus. A first point is not discerned of beings roaming and wandering on, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving. There may come a time, bhikkhus, when the great ocean dries up, completely vanishes, and is no more. But still, bhikkhus, I say that there is no end of suffering for beings roaming and wandering on, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving. There may come a time, bhikkhus, when Sineru, the king of mountains, erodes, perishes, and is no more. But still, bhikkhus, I say that there is no end of suffering for beings roaming and wandering on, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving! There may come a time, bhikkhus, when the great earth erodes, perishes, and is no more. But still, bhikkhus, I say that there is no end of suffering for beings roaming and wandering on, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving!

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.99

item.title: Bhikkhus, regarding the precepts that are unbroken, unblemished, unspotted, untarnished, leading to liberation, praised by the wise, not clung to, conducive to concentration — a…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, regarding the precepts that are unbroken, unblemished, unspotted, untarnished, leading to liberation, praised by the wise, not clung to, conducive to concentration — a bhikkhu lives possessing such precepts in common with his fellow celibates, both in private and in public. This principle of cordiality creates affection, creates respect, leading to cohesion, to non-dispute, to harmony, to unity.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 48 – Kosambiyasutta

item.title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, good associates. This, bhikkhus, is a quality that constitutes a guardian. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is…
item.description:
Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, good associates. This, bhikkhus, is a quality that constitutes a guardian. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is easy to speak to, possessing qualities that make him easy to admonish, patient, and well-receptive to instruction. This, bhikkhus, is a quality that constitutes a guardian. Furthermore, bhikkhus, for whatever duties his fellow celibates have to do, whether great or small, he is skillful and diligent, possessing the right consideration of means, able to do and to organize. This, bhikkhus, is a quality that constitutes a guardian. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu loves the Dhamma, speaks pleasantly, rejoices greatly in the supreme Dhamma and supreme Discipline. This, bhikkhus, is a quality that constitutes a guardian.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.17
